# A. The Question {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Some jobs have no fixed time. Only a **finish line**. 🏁

## Drive until the black line

```{.python}
left.run(300)
wait(????)     # how long??
left.stop()
```

::: {.qbox}
[How long do you wait before `stop()`?]{.qtitle}
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .teal}
Nobody knows. So don't guess: **keep checking.** Keep driving *while* the line is not there yet.
:::
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
The robot's eye comes later. Today the finish line is a **wheel angle**.
:::

::: {.notes}
Let them answer with a number first. Someone will say "2000", someone "3500". Ask: what if the robot starts further back? What if the battery is low? The time changes every run, so no number is right. That is the whole reason `while` exists: it repeats until something becomes true, however long that takes. Keep this slide to two minutes. This session assumes only D2 (imports, `Motor`, `run_angle`, variables). The next slide hands them the five motor words the loops need, and no `for` loop is needed anywhere; `for` arrives in *Drive a Square*.
:::

## Five new words 🔤

| Code | What it does |
|:--|:--|
| `left.run(300)` | start turning at 300 °/s, **and keep going** |
| `left.stop()` | stop turning |
| `left.reset_angle(0)` | call this spot **0°** |
| `left.angle()` | how far it has turned since 0° |
| `print(x)` | show `x` in the console |

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .purple}
`run_angle` stops by itself. `run` **never** does. Something else has to call `stop()`, at the right moment.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Two minutes, no robots yet. `run_angle` from D2 is "go this far, then stop"; `run` is "go, and I will tell you when to stop". That missing "when" is the whole session. `print` is new too: point at the console pane in the Pybricks editor so they know where the numbers will appear. If someone asks how `run_angle` knows when to stop: "it runs a loop just like the one you are about to write". That is true, and it is a good hook.
:::

# B. Watch a Loop Think {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #625D9C)"}

Step through it **one line at a time**. 👣

## Meet `while`

Predict: **how many lines will it print?** Then press Step.

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .purple}
**Check → body → jump back → check again.** It leaves the moment the check says False.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Collect predictions on the board before anyone presses anything: "3", "4", "2" are all common. Then Step slowly and have the room say each line out loud before you press. The lamp on the right is the heart of it: every time the highlight lands on the `while` line, the check is asked again and the lamp shows the answer. Point out the jump back up after `count = count + 1`, which is the only thing that makes a loop a loop. It prints 0, 1, 2, then "done": four lines, and the body ran 3 times. The fourth check is the one people forget: it is the False that lets the program leave.
:::

```{=html}
  </div>

      <div class="wl-ln" id="s2L2">    print(count)</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s2L3">    count = count + 1</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s2L4">print("done")</div>
    </div>
    <div class="wl-side">
      <div class="wl-lamp" id="s2Lamp">check: not yet</div>
      <div class="wl-stats"><span>count <b id="s2Count">?</b></span><span>body ran <b id="s2Runs">0</b> times</span></div>

```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .teal}
With `< 0` the body runs **zero** times. The check always comes **first**.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Go `< 5` first (easy win: five prints), then `< 0`. Most students predict one print for `< 0` because "the loop runs at least once". It does not: the very first check is `0 < 0`, which is False, so Python skips the body and goes straight to "done". Say the rule: a `while` asks before it acts. This matters on the robot: if the wheel is already past the finish line, a `while` drive does nothing at all, which is correct.
:::

## 🐛 Bug hunt: the missing colon

::: {.qbox}
[This loop won't even start. Pybricks flags the **first line** in red. What's missing?]{.qtitle}
:::

```python
count = 0
while count < 3
    print(count)
    count = count + 1
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
`SyntaxError`: no **colon**. Every loop header ends in `:`, which says *"the block starts here."* Fix: `while count < 3:`
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The colon is invisible until it's missing. Type it live so the red SyntaxError lands on the `while` line. Make the habit loud: say "colon" out loud every time anyone types a loop header this week. It is the number-one typo of the session, and `for` will have exactly the same rule in *Drive a Square*.
:::

## 🐛 Bug hunt: the runaway line

::: {.qbox}
[The colon is back, and it *still* won't run. The error points at **line 3**.]{.qtitle}
:::

```python
count = 0
while count < 3:
print(count)
count = count + 1
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
`IndentationError`: lines inside a loop must be **pushed in** (one Tab). The spaces tell Python what repeats.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Indentation-as-meaning is the single biggest beginner hurdle, so spend a beat. Show flush-left (crashes) next to indented (runs). Then the sneaky version: indent **only** `print(count)`. No crash, but `count = count + 1` now sits outside the loop, so the body never changes what the check reads. That is exactly the next slide, so let the frozen console land and go straight on.
:::

## Break it: the loop that never ends 🥶

Delete one line. **Predict, then Run.**

```{=html}
<div class="sim">
  <div class="sim-controls">
    <button class="sim-btn small on" data-sim="wlSet" data-sim-arg="s3:inc"><span class="wl-mono">count = count + 1</span> ✓</button>
    <button class="sim-btn small ghost" data-sim="wlSet" data-sim-arg="s3:noinc">delete it ✂️</button>
    <span class="sim-tag">·</span>
    <button class="sim-btn small" data-sim="wlRun" data-sim-arg="s3">▶ Run</button>
    <button class="sim-btn coral small" data-sim="wlHalt" data-sim-arg="s3">⏹ Stop</button>
    <button class="sim-btn ghost small" data-sim="wlReset" data-sim-arg="s3">↺ Reset</button>
  </div>
  <div class="sim-stage">
    <div class="wl-code">
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s3L0">count = 0</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s3L1">while count &lt; <span id="s3N">3</span>:</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s3L2">    print(count)</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s3L3">    count = count + 1</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="s3L4">print("done")</div>
    </div>
    <div class="wl-side">
      <div class="wl-lamp" id="s3Lamp">check: not yet</div>
      <div class="wl-stats"><span>count <b id="s3Count">?</b></span><span>body ran <b id="s3Runs">0</b> times</span></div>
      <div class="wl-con" id="s3Con"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="sim-msg" id="s3Msg"></div>
</div>
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
The check reads `count`. Nothing changes `count`. **The body must change what the check reads.**
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Run it once with the line in place (it ends), then delete it and run again. Let it spin: the counter races, the console floods with 0s, and the check number climbs into the hundreds. Ask: "when will it stop?" (Never.) Press Stop and tie it to the hub: on the robot, the centre button is your Stop. Then the rule on the card. Every frozen loop they will ever write breaks this rule: the check is waiting for a change that nothing in the body makes. On the robot, the "change" usually comes from the world: a wheel turning, a gyro moving. That is the next section.
:::

# C. Now With a Wheel {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

Same loop. Now the check reads a **motor**. ⚙️

## Drive to the finish line 🏁

Two full turns = **720°**. Where will the wheel stop?

```{=html}
<div class="sim">
  <div class="sim-controls">
    <button class="sim-btn" data-sim="wlWheel" data-sim-arg="w1">▶ Run</button>
    <button class="sim-btn ghost" data-sim="wlWheelReset" data-sim-arg="w1">↺ Reset</button>
  </div>
  <div class="sim-stage">
    <div class="wl-code">
      <div class="wl-ln" id="w1L0">left.reset_angle(0)</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="w1L1">left.run(300)</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="w1L2">while left.angle() &lt; 720:</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="w1L3">    wait(<span id="w1W">10</span>)</div>
      <div class="wl-ln" id="w1L4">left.stop()</div>
    </div>
    <div class="wl-side">
      <div class="wl-wheel">
        <svg width="120" height="120" viewBox="-50 -50 100 100">
          <circle r="44" fill="#1C355E"/><circle r="30" fill="#eef3f8"/>
          <g id="w1Spin"><rect x="-4" y="-30" width="8" height="60" fill="#625D9C"/><rect x="-30" y="-4" width="60" height="8" fill="#625D9C"/><circle cy="-37" r="5" fill="#FFD500"/></g>
        </svg>
        <div class="wl-stats" style="flex-direction:column;gap:4px;"><span>angle <b id="w1Ang">0</b>°</span><span>checks <b id="w1Chk">0</b></span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="wl-lamp" id="w1Lamp">check: not yet</div>
      <div>
        <div class="wl-track"><div class="wl-fill" id="w1Fill"></div><div class="wl-finish" style="left:72%"></div><div id="w1Dots"></div></div>
        <div class="wl-scale"><span>0°</span><span>720° 🏁</span><span>1000°</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="sim-msg" id="w1Msg"></div>
</div>
```

::: {.notes}
Same four ideas as the counter: something to read (`left.angle()`), a check (`< 720`), a body (`wait(10)`), and a change. The difference is who makes the change: not a line of code, but the motor, which keeps turning on its own because `left.run(300)` started it before the loop. The body only waits. Each dot on the track is one check, and at `wait(10)` they are so close together they look like a solid line. It stops at 720 exactly. Keep that number in mind: slide 3 of this section breaks it.
:::

This is the robot version of the frozen counter, and it is the most common real bug of the week: the program "hangs", the robot sits still, and students think the hub crashed. It did not crash; it is checking hundreds of times a second, and the answer never changes. Ask "what should change the angle?" and let them find the missing `run`. On the real hub, the centre button stops it.
:::

```{=html}
        </svg>

```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .purple}
The loop only looks at the top. Between checks the wheel keeps going. **Short wait, sharp stop.**
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Take a prediction for each wait before running it. Most students expect every version to stop at 720, because "the code says 720". Run 10 ms (720), then 250 ms (750, 30° late), then 1000 ms (900, a full 180° late). The dots on the track are the only moments the loop was looking: at `wait(1000)` it checks at 0, 300, 600 and 900, and it cannot notice the finish line in between. The check only happens at the top of the loop, and a long body means long blind spots. That is why every robot loop in this course keeps its body short, `wait(10)` or less. The sim ignores momentum on purpose; the bench slide brings it back.
:::

# D. On Purpose {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

One loop that never ends **on purpose**, then your own wheel. ♾️

## Forever, on purpose ♾️

```{.python}
while True:
    print(left.angle())
    wait(100)
```

`True` is a check that can never be False. The hub's **centre button** ends it.

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .teal}
Patrols and line followers work this way: **keep going until a human says stop.**
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Short slide. The frozen loops earlier were accidents; this one is a choice. It is also the best debugging tool they have: run it, turn the wheel by hand and watch the angle stream. Have one student try it on a robot now if time allows. Later decks (line following, patrol) put real work inside `while True`.
:::

## Bench: stop at one turn 🤖

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="|5|6-9|10-11"}
from pybricks.pupdevices import Motor
from pybricks.parameters import Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
left = Motor(Port.F)     # yours
left.reset_angle(0)
left.run(300)
while left.angle() < 360:
    wait(10)
left.stop()
wait(500)
print(left.angle())
```
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
1. Run it. **What does it print?**
2. Make it **3 turns**.
3. **Halve the speed.** Does the extra shrink?

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
The sim stopped right on the line. Yours went **past**. The loop caught 360 on time, so who stole the extra degrees? **Hold that thought** for *Drive a Square*.
:::
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Robots out, one wheel lifted off the table or the robot on its back so it does not drive away. Expect prints like 370 to 390 at speed 300: the loop caught the finish line within a few degrees, then the wheel coasted. The `wait(500)` before the print lets the coast finish, otherwise they read the angle mid-coast. Halving the speed should shrink the extra, which proves it is not the loop. Coach knowledge only: it is momentum. **Do not name it today.** *Drive a Square* names it on the gyro ("it printed 94, who's guilty?"), and that reveal only works if the room has not heard the word yet. If a team gets a frozen program, send them back to the two "break it" slides: is the check reading something that changes? Port F follows the course robot; students change it to match their own build. `Direction` is left out on purpose: a lone wheel counts positive degrees for `run(300)` whichever way it is mounted.
:::

## You're done when…

::: {.callout-important}
## Done when
- You can **predict** how many times any `while` body runs (zero counts)
- You can **fix** a loop that never ends, and say what never changed
- You can **fix** a missing colon or a runaway line
- Your wheel **stops at one turn**, and you can say the extra is **not** the loop's fault
:::

::: {.notes}
Check each leg orally at the bench. For leg one, write `while count < 4:` with `count = 1` on the board and ask for the number of prints (3). For leg two, show a `while left.angle() < 360: wait(10)` with no `run` above it and ask what is wrong. For leg three, hand them a header with no colon and a body typed flush-left. For leg four, ask why the printed angle is bigger than 360: "the wheel kept going after `stop()`" is a pass; the word *momentum* waits for *Drive a Square*.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
  /* ---------- The counter stepper (s1, s2, s3) ---------- */
  var S = {
    s1: {n:3, inc:true},
    s2: {n:3, inc:true},
    s3: {n:3, inc:true}
  };
  function fresh(k){
    var s = S[k];
    s.pc = 0; s.count = null; s.runs = 0; s.checks = 0; s.out = []; s.done = false; s.last = -1;
  }
  function hi(k, line){
    for(var i=0;i<5;i++){ var e = SIM.el(k+'L'+i); if(e) e.classList.toggle('on', i===line); }
  }
  function draw(k){
    var s = S[k];
    hi(k, s.last);
    SIM.text(k+'Count', s.count===null ? '?' : String(s.count));
    SIM.text(k+'Runs', String(s.runs));
    SIM.text(k+'Con', s.out.slice(-6).join('\n'));
  }
  function lamp(k, text, val){
    var e = SIM.el(k+'Lamp'); if(!e) return;
    e.textContent = text;
    e.classList.remove('t','f');
    if(val===true) e.classList.add('t');
    if(val===false) e.classList.add('f');
  }
  function reset(k){
    SIM.stop(k);
    fresh(k);
    var s = S[k];
    SIM.text(k+'N', String(s.n));
    var l3 = SIM.el(k+'L3');
    if(l3){
      l3.textContent = s.inc ? '    count = count + 1' : '    # count = count + 1';
      l3.classList.toggle('gone', !s.inc);
    }
    lamp(k, 'check: not yet', null);
    SIM.msg(k+'Msg', '', null);
    draw(k);
  }
  /* One line of the program. Returns true when the program has ended. */
  function step(k){
    var s = S[k];
    if(s.done) return true;
    var line = s.pc;
    if(line===0){ s.count = 0; s.pc = 1; }
    else if(line===1){
      s.checks++;
      var ok = s.count < s.n;
      lamp(k, 'check #'+s.checks+':  '+s.count+' < '+s.n+'  →  '+(ok?'True':'False'), ok);
      s.pc = ok ? 2 : 4;
      if(!s.inc && s.checks > 4) SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'Still True. Check #'+s.checks+'. Nothing in the body changes <code>count</code>.', 'bad');
    }
    else if(line===2){ s.out.push(String(s.count)); s.runs++; s.pc = s.inc ? 3 : 1; }
    else if(line===3){ s.count = s.count + 1; s.pc = 1; }
    else if(line===4){
      s.out.push('done'); s.done = true;
      if(s.runs===0) SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'The first check was False, so the body ran 0 times.', 'note');
      else SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'The body ran '+s.runs+' times. Check #'+s.checks+' said False, so the loop ended.', 'good');
    }
    s.last = line;
    draw(k);
    return s.done;
  }
  SIM.def('wlStep', function(k){ SIM.stop(k); step(k); });   // after "done", Reset starts over
  SIM.def('wlReset', function(k){ reset(k); });
  SIM.def('wlHalt', function(k){
    if(!S[k].done && S[k].pc!==0){
      SIM.stop(k);
      SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'You stopped it at check #'+S[k].checks+'. On the hub, the centre button does this.', 'note');
    }
  });
  SIM.def('wlRun', function(k){
    reset(k);
    var s = S[k], acc = 0, rate = 4;
    SIM.loop(k, {
      dt: 0.01,
      step: function(dt){
        acc += dt * rate;
        if(!s.inc) rate = Math.min(rate * 1.004, 60);   // the runaway speeds up
        while(acc >= 1){
          acc -= 1;
          if(step(k)) return true;
          if(s.checks >= 999){
            SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'We stopped it at check #999. The robot never would have.', 'bad');
            return true;
          }
        }
        return false;
      }
    });
  });
  SIM.def('wlSet', function(arg, btn){
    var p = String(arg).split(':'), k = p[0], v = p[1], s = S[k];
    if(v.slice(0,2)==='lt') s.n = Number(v.slice(2));
    if(v==='inc') s.inc = true;
    if(v==='noinc') s.inc = false;
    if(btn && btn.parentNode){
      btn.parentNode.querySelectorAll('[data-sim="wlSet"]').forEach(function(b){
        b.classList.toggle('on', b===btn); b.classList.toggle('ghost', b!==btn);
      });
    }
    reset(k);
  });
  ['s1','s2','s3'].forEach(reset);

  /* ---------- The wheel (w1, w2, w3) ---------- */
  var SPEED = 300, FINISH = 720, SCALE = 1000;
  var W = {
    w1: {w:10, run:true},
    w2: {w:10, run:true},
    w3: {w:10, run:true}
  };
  function pct(a){ return Math.min(a, SCALE) / SCALE * 100; }
  function wheelDraw(k, ang, checks){
    SIM.tf(k+'Spin', 'rotate('+(ang % 360).toFixed(1)+')');
    SIM.text(k+'Ang', String(Math.round(ang)));
    SIM.text(k+'Chk', String(checks));
    var f = SIM.el(k+'Fill'); if(f) f.style.width = pct(ang)+'%';
  }
  function dot(k, a, ok){
    var box = SIM.el(k+'Dots'); if(!box) return;
    var d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className = ok ? 'wl-dot' : 'wl-dot f';
    d.style.left = pct(a)+'%';
    box.appendChild(d);
  }
  function wheelReset(k){
    SIM.stop(k);
    var s = W[k];
    SIM.text(k+'W', String(s.w));
    var l1 = SIM.el(k+'L1');
    if(l1){
      l1.textContent = s.run ? 'left.run(300)' : '# left.run(300)';
      l1.classList.toggle('gone', !s.run);
    }
    for(var i=0;i<5;i++){ var e = SIM.el(k+'L'+i); if(e) e.classList.remove('on'); }
    var box = SIM.el(k+'Dots'); if(box) box.innerHTML = '';
    lamp(k, 'check: not yet', null);
    SIM.msg(k+'Msg', '', null);
    wheelDraw(k, 0, 0);
  }
  SIM.def('wlWheelReset', function(k){ wheelReset(k); });
  SIM.def('wlWheelHalt', function(k){
    if(W[k].live){
      SIM.stop(k); W[k].live = false;
      SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'You stopped it. The angle never moved, so the check was always True.', 'note');
    }
  });
  SIM.def('wlWheelSet', function(arg, btn){
    var p = String(arg).split(':'), k = p[0], v = p[1], s = W[k];
    if(v==='run') s.run = true;
    if(v==='norun') s.run = false;
    if(v.charAt(0)==='w') s.w = Number(v.slice(1));
    if(btn && btn.parentNode){
      btn.parentNode.querySelectorAll('[data-sim="wlWheelSet"]').forEach(function(b){
        b.classList.toggle('on', b===btn); b.classList.toggle('ghost', b!==btn);
      });
    }
    wheelReset(k);
  });
  SIM.def('wlWheel', function(k){
    wheelReset(k);
    var s = W[k], t = 0, n = 0, ang = 0, checks = 0, stopAt = null;
    s.live = true;
    var speed = s.run ? SPEED : 0;
    SIM.loop(k, {
      dt: 0.005,
      step: function(dt){
        // Checks happen at t = n * wait. Integer maths keeps 720 exactly 720.
        if(t >= n * s.w / 1000){
          var a = speed * n * s.w / 1000;
          checks++;
          var ok = a < FINISH;
          dot(k, a, ok);
          lamp(k, 'check #'+checks+':  '+Math.round(a)+' < '+FINISH+'  →  '+(ok?'True':'False'), ok);
          if(!ok){ stopAt = a; ang = a; return true; }
          n++;
          if(!s.run && t > 6){ return true; }
        }
        t += dt;
        ang = speed * t;
        return false;
      },
      draw: function(){
        wheelDraw(k, ang, checks);
        hi(k, stopAt===null ? 3 : 4);
        if(!s.run && checks > 5 && stopAt===null) SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'Still True. The wheel is not turning, so the angle never changes.', 'bad');
      },
      done: function(){
        s.live = false;
        if(stopAt===null){
          SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'We stopped it after '+checks+' checks. The robot never would have.', 'bad');
          return;
        }
        var over = Math.round(stopAt - FINISH), gap = SPEED * s.w / 1000;
        if(over===0) SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'Stopped at '+Math.round(stopAt)+'°, right on the line. Checks were '+gap+'° apart.', 'good');
        else SIM.msg(k+'Msg', 'Stopped at '+Math.round(stopAt)+'°: '+over+'° past the line. Checks were '+gap+'° apart.', 'bad');
      }
    });
  });
  ['w1','w2','w3'].forEach(wheelReset);
})();
</script>
```
